title: Alpenmess in Singapore
subtitle: A sales and service office, read before it opens
note: Alpenmess is an example name for an example company: a Swiss maker of precision measuring instruments and calibration software for semiconductor and electronics factories, opening in Singapore to sell across Southeast Asia. Every finding is an Antevo engine's answer on the date shown; where a desk named a company, the page describes it instead.

tries.label: The plan, piece by piece
tries.source: Antevo Trademark, Antevo Research (economy and geopolitics desks), Antevo Strategy Radar, Antevo Executive Brief and Antevo Tremor Watch, 25 Nov 2026 · trademark registers, the .ch, .com and .sg registries. items.name: The name in Singapore
evidence: No near marks found in classes 9, 37 and 42, in Singapore or the other registers searched
No entity under the name in Singapore's register (ACRA) or in Switzerland's
alpenmess.sg, .ch and .com appear unregistered

items.name: Demand
evidence: Singapore's 2026 growth forecast was raised to around 6% on 24 November; 6.1% a year on in the third quarter
Electronics exports rose 73.9% a year on in October
A major US inspection-equipment maker opened its largest plant worldwide in Singapore on 20 November
The 2027 guide is 2.5% to 4.5%, as AI investment is expected to cool

items.name: Trade rules
evidence: The EFTA free trade agreement with Singapore has been in force since 2003; instruments move without tariffs
A US rule published on 19 November puts advanced AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia under licence, with a 90-day window to about 17 February 2027
Instruments with US-origin parts or software can carry US export rules when they are resold from Singapore into the region

items.name: An export licence from Switzerland
evidence: Metrology for advanced chip production can count as dual-use (Wassenaar category 3) and need a licence from SECO
Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam and Thailand are not embargoed, so licences are generally grantable, with end-user declarations

items.name: The franc
evidence: One franc bought about 1.55 Singapore dollars on 25 November
The franc is 3.4% stronger against the dollar than a year ago, so prices set in francs look dearer locally
The Monetary Authority of Singapore held its policy in October; its next review is in January

steps.label: Before the office opens, with the links

items.do: Classify each product for export control, in Switzerland and for US-origin parts
items.why: This is the one step that can stop a shipment: a SECO licence for dual-use metrology, and US rules on resale from Singapore if US parts or software are inside.

items.do: File the name in Singapore in classes 9, 37 and 42, then watch it
items.why: The screen is clear today; a filing protects the name, and a watch catches the next close mark.

items.do: Register the Singapore company and secure alpenmess.sg
items.why: No entity uses the name in Singapore's register, and the domain appears free; both can change at any time.

items.do: Write end-user undertakings into every distributor contract
items.why: Swiss and US rules can follow an instrument resold from Singapore to a third country.

items.do: Decide the invoicing currency before the first quote
items.why: With the franc strong, quotes in francs look dearer locally; the January review sets the Singapore dollar's path.

items.do: Plan work passes for the first hires, and talk to the trade promoters
items.why: Service engineers on site need passes; the Swiss and Singapore trade agencies know the region's buyers.

sections.title: The region's demand
sections.so_what: Factories that are installed now need calibration and repair for years, so a service office earns from the installed base even if new orders slow in 2027.
evidence: Manufacturing, mainly electronics and precision engineering, carries Singapore's growth; retail fell 2.7% a year on in the third quarter
Malaysia is the region's other chip hub; Vietnam's electronics assembly is growing as supply chains move out of China
Core inflation in Singapore eased to 1.5% in October

sections.title: The rules around the customers
sections.so_what: Customers in Malaysia and Thailand will screen their suppliers harder in 2027: expect longer sales cycles and questions about where each part comes from.
evidence: The US-China trade truce formally expires on 10 January 2027
A deeper China-ASEAN trade agreement enters into force on 1 December 2026, easing access for Chinese instrument makers
Singapore chairs ASEAN in 2027

sections.title: What changed for companies today
sections.so_what: Both reach Alpenmess through its customers: chip factories that depend on AI funding, and equipment bought from economies named in the reported US tariff plans.
evidence: The AI relief rally reversed in a day; one weak bond or share sale could hit chip and power orders (high impact, medium likelihood, rising)
Washington is reported to be readying higher tariffs on China, the EU, Japan, South Korea and a dozen more economies; rates and dates are not published

sections.title: Markets this week
sections.so_what: Not a reason to delay, but a reason not to fix a currency or a lease on a single day.
evidence: Week of 20 November, down from high the week before
Bonds, commodities and volatility breaking; credit and currencies calm
sections.source: Antevo Tremor Watch, week of 20 Nov 2026

links.text: The name is clear in Singapore, and the desk finds demand strong: the order to act in is name, company, then the first hires.
The US chip rule and the AI funding strain are one risk seen twice: both slow new factories, neither empties the installed base a service office lives on.
A strong franc and elevated markets argue for deciding the invoicing currency once, not at each quote.

watch: The deeper China-ASEAN trade agreement in force on 1 December 2026
The G-20 summit in mid-December and any extension of the US-China truce
The truce's formal expiry on 10 January 2027
The Monetary Authority of Singapore's review in January 2027
The US chip licensing window closing around 17 February 2027
New marks close to the name (Antevo Trademark watch)
